evidence: A section reference takes the form § N.M (the thin space after § is optional, so §7.3 and § 7.3 name the same reference), which means Chapter N, Section M — so § 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement), not Section 1's fourth subsection.
issue: Preface defines § N.M as Chapter N, Section M, but then exempts itself: '§ 1.4 is Ch. 1, Section 4 (Measurement)' assumes Section 4 exists and is titled Measurement in Ch 1. Body Ch 1 Table of Contents lists Ch 1 as 'It All Starts With the First Token' with no explicit Section 4 label visible in excerpt. Convention not verifiable within provided pages and risks bare § references flagged under mandatory pass 2.
fix_instruction: Add a resolved example that exists in body (e.g., §2.3 or §4.3) and ensure List of Contents includes section numbers/titles so § N.M can be verified to resolve; audit all bare §7 occurrences for missing .M.

evidence: GPU memory, VRAM and HBM are used interchangeably for accelerator-local memory — the same pool under three names: the worked examples write "GPU memory" or "VRAM" for a capacity and "HBM" for the technology, and never mean two different pools by the switch.
issue: Terminology synonym declaration is in Preface only; body Chapter 2 and Chapter 4 repeatedly switch between HBM bandwidth (3.35 TB/s) and GPU memory capacity without re-stating the synonym rule. Per blind spot on GPU memory/VRAM/HBM terminology, a reader entering at Ch 2 may misread HBM as separate pool from VRAM, affecting KV budget vs bandwidth checks.
fix_instruction: Repeat 1-sentence synonym reminder in Chapter 2 §2.1 resource model table footnote and in Chapter 7 intro where capacity vs bandwidth are contrasted.

evidence: The canonical model is a constructed full-MHA teaching geometry (80 layers, hidden size 8192), not a named vendor checkpoint; Ch. 4's "CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL" callout states the intent: GQA/MQA and sparse attention shrink the KV constant several-fold in 2026 production models, so the book's ∼2.62 MB/token is a deliberate upper bound (the derivation: 2 × 80 × 8192 × 2 B = 2,621,440 B = 2.62 MB per token at FP16, one K and one V tensor per layer; grouped-query attention scales that by nKV-heads/nheads).
issue: KV MB/token arithmetic itself recomputes correctly (2*80*8192*2=2,621,440 B ≈2.62 MB), but label scope is ambiguous per blind spot: Preface calls it 'deliberate upper bound' while Chapters 1-2 use the same 2.62 MB/token as KV budget without re-flagging [CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL][ASSUMPTION] vs [1P][FACT]. Risk of treating illustrative bound as measured per-model fact in fleet sizing.
fix_instruction: On every KV budget table (Ch 2 Table 2-2, Ch 4 budget, Appendix A) append provenance tag [CANONICAL TEACHING MODEL][ASSUMPTION][DERIVED] and footnote 'Not a vendor KV-head count; re-derive via nKV-heads/nheads for target model'.

evidence: TTFTe2e = retrieval + admission/queue + tokenization/transfer + prefill, where tokenization/transfer counts as one combined term. The sum carries no separate "first decode step" term: prefill samples the first token, so a term for that work would count it twice. The canonical 1.2 s budget covers only the two dominant modeled terms (retrieval ∼120 ms + prefill ∼1.08 s); admission/queue and tokenization/transfer sit outside that 1.2 s figure.
issue: TTFT 4-term definition vs 2-term budget restatement is technically consistent (B_other outside budget), but the phrasing 'covers only the two dominant modeled terms' invites misreading the 1.2 s as full TTFT SLO while later chapters test against it as if it were full TTFT. Per blind spot on TTFT 4-term vs 2-term, a stale budget comparison can pass when admission/queue would breach SLO.
fix_instruction: Rename canonical figure to 'TTFT_modelled = retrieval + prefill =1.2 s (budget_prefill ≤1.08 s − B_other)' and require every 'meets 1.2 s' claim to cite B_other measurement status (ANALYTICAL vs MEASURED) per Ch 14 protocol.
